Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

death penalty noun

also capital punishment, execution, condemn to death, death sentence, receive the death sentence, put to death, execute (a criminal)

classical

Traupman 194

supplicium capitis

the death penalty

Supplicium alone is often the death penalty; caput, the head, is one’s life and civil standing, so a capital charge is rēs capitālis and to condemn to death is capitis damnāre, with the genitive.

Other words

  • ultimum supplicium — the extreme penalty

    also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.84 (Lewis & Short s.v. supplicium)

Examples

  • aliquem capitis damnāre

    to condemn someone to deathTraupman 194; cf. Caes. BC 3.83.4 (Lewis & Short s.v. damnō)

  • capitis damnārī

    to receive the death sentenceTraupman 194

  • suppliciō capitis afficī

    to suffer capital punishmentTraupman 194; cf. Caes. BG 1.27: suppliciō afficī, to be put to death (Lewis & Short s.v. supplicium)

  • supplicium capitis dē aliquō sūmere

    to put someone to deathTraupman 194

See also punishment, punish, kill.
